files.name: CHANGELOG.md
files.body:
### Fixed
- **The file index grew by one row per path at every scan for files reached through a share** (Fix [#198](https://github.com/eldertek/duplicatefinder/issues/198)). The owner stored in a row is the owner of the file, but the row was looked up with the user who runs the scan, so for a shared path the existing row was never found and each scan inserted another one (4 scans, 4 rows per path). `occ duplicates:list-all` and the duplicate lists then showed the same path several times. The row of a path is now found by its path when the scanning user is not its owner, and the rows already in surplus (same path, same owner) are removed once after the update, by the repair step and then by the clean-up job. Checked on Nextcloud 28 and 34 with a folder shared between two users and three scans in a row: the number of rows stays the same
- Files skipped by the setting `ignore_mounted_files` were logged as errors ("Failed to handle file info event") on each run of the duplicate search, which kept the "Errors in the log" warning of the admin overview on, and the exception stopped the hashing of the other files of the same size (Fix [#199](https://github.com/eldertek/duplicatefinder/issues/199)). They are now skipped one by one, without any log line

### Changed
- **Faster scans** (PR [#190](https://github.com/eldertek/duplicatefinder/pull/190) by teddy0605, thank you). Folders are no longer stored in the file index (a repair step removes the folder rows already stored, by windows of ids so that the update stays short on large tables), files that are alone with their size are not processed again at each scan, the ignore rules and the `.nodupefinder` lookups are cached during a scan, and files that are already indexed and unchanged are skipped. Measured by the author on an instance of 240 000 files: the search job went from 6-7 hours to 157 seconds, with the same rows, hashes and groups after a scan. A filter added while a scan runs is seen from the next scan
